A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DepthCues study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing experiments across 20 vision models, depth-cue analyses, and fine-tuning results on NYUv2 and DIW, with additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds DIW correlation results, repeated-seed fine-tuning evaluations, and comparisons of relative and metric depth checkpoints.

M1.justification: Feature pooling and differencing, MLP and attentive probes, and LoRA fine-tuning remain unchanged. The added statement that the backbone is frozen during probing reiterates information already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six DepthCues tasks and constituent datasets, NYUv2, DIW, and ImageNet-1k. The additional DIW analysis and checkpoint comparisons reuse existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table A5 evaluates indoor and outdoor metric DepthAnythingv2 checkpoints against the relative-depth version. The 20 primary models and the existing appendix evaluations of DepthAnything and MoGe are retained.

E3.justification: No revisions to data splits, preprocessing, probes, layer-selection rules, evaluation metrics, or training budgets are reported. The added checkpoint comparison uses the existing DepthCues evaluation framework; additional seed repetitions are assessed under E5.

E4.justification: v2 adds a DepthCues–DIW correlation analysis in Figure A2 and a relative-versus-metric checkpoint analysis in Table A5. Existing probe ablations, layer searches, model-family analyses, and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.5 explicitly reports repeating both fine-tuning and evaluation with three random seeds, adding aggregate scores and variability in Table A4. Figure A1 also gains R-squared and p-value reporting. The original five-seed DepthCues protocol is unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and Table 2 values are retained. Added results include DIW correlation with R-squared 0.80, relative/metric checkpoint scores, and three-seed outcomes. For example, new Table A4 reports CLIP DIW WHDR of 35.33 (0.09), versus 32.69 (0.98) with concatenated original and fine-tuned features.

T1.justification: The mathematical task definitions, feature-extraction equations, depth-accuracy formula, and LoRA equations are unchanged. No theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a six-cue benchmark, evaluation of 20 models, emergence of human-like depth cues, and potential depth-estimation benefits from DepthCues fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly explains that the metric checkpoints’ generally lower performance could reflect fine-tuning on smaller datasets, leaving the cause for future investigation. Earlier limitations and failure-case interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 newly identifies the previously evaluated DepthAnythingv2 checkpoint as the relative-depth version and describes the metric checkpoints as indoor/outdoor fine-tuned derivatives. Existing hyperparameters, hardware/runtime estimates, dataset-construction details, and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work positioning and set of 88 cited works remain unchanged. Lexicon3D receives a publication-metadata update from arXiv to NeurIPS; removing CLIP from one introductory example list does not redefine the paper’s contribution.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify frozen features, remove CLIP from one introductory example list, update bibliographic metadata, and expand acknowledgments. Short appendix passages describe the additional analyses; the main narrative and section hierarchy remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure A2 and Tables A4–A5, and updates Figure A1 with a fitted line, statistics, and revised axis wording. Appendix displays are reflowed and renumbered, including old Table A4 becoming A6; the main figures retain their design.

improvement.justification: The three-seed fine-tuning evaluations provide stronger support for previously reported benefits, while the DIW correlation analysis broadens validation using an existing dataset. The checkpoint comparison adds useful evidence and explicitly acknowledges its training-data confound. These are limited improvements in evidential support and documentation; the core benchmark, method, and conclusions remain stable.
